_about: Example curated stream splits. Copy to a real splits.json at cutover. Each entry cuts one or more blue lines at one location. from_dict ignores _comment/_about fields. See splits.schema.md.

splits._comment: PRIMARY FORM: a single coordinate + one blue line. Snap the point to the nearest point on that BLK and cut there. Use for a dam, gauge, bridge, or any hand-picked spot on one channel.
splits.label: Squilax bridge

splits._comment: PRIMARY FORM (multi-cut): a single coordinate + a WATERSHED CODE. Snap the point to the nearest point on EACH blue line sharing that WSC (main channel + all side channels) and cut them all at that location. This is how you split a braided river (e.g. the Fraser) cleanly across every channel at a section/zone boundary.
splits.label: Zone 2/3 boundary

splits._comment: LAKE: cut where the stream enters/exits a lake. Target the named river; anchor the lake by waterbody_key. Produces the 'upstream of Adams Lake' / 'downstream of Adams Lake' sections automatically.
splits.label: Adams Lake

splits._comment: EXACT: cut at a specific linear_feature_id boundary (used today for Wigwam/Shuswap in overrides.json). No snapping — deterministic.
splits.label: the divide

splits._comment: MU BOUNDARY: cut where the stream crosses a management-unit boundary (curated, only where specific regs differ per zone). Behaves like a point cut located at the crossing.
splits.label: Zone 2 / Zone 3

splits._comment: BARRIER: a flow barrier (dam) — cuts geometry AND stops upstream tributary propagation (becomes a topology barrier node).
splits.label: the dam
